overview: Honduras is a country in Central America, between Guatemala, El Salvador and Nicaragua. Its capital and largest city is Tegucigalpa. Honduras became independent from Spain in 1821. The ancient Maya city of Copán, in the west of the country, is famous for its carved stone monuments.

geography.text: Honduras is mostly mountainous, with a long Caribbean coastline in the north and a short Pacific coast on the Gulf of Fonseca in the south. Off the north coast lie the Bay Islands, surrounded by coral reefs. The east, called La Mosquitia, is a remote region of rainforest and wetlands.

history.text: The Maya city of Copán flourished in western Honduras. Spain conquered the area in the 1500s, and Honduras became independent in 1821. In the 1900s US fruit companies became so powerful there that it was nicknamed a 'banana republic'. Hurricane Mitch devastated the country in 1998.

government.text: Honduras is a presidential republic. The President is elected every four years. In 2009 the army removed President Manuel Zelaya, causing a political crisis. Xiomara Castro became its first female President in 2022.

economy.text: Honduras is one of the poorer countries in Latin America. It exports coffee, bananas, palm oil, shrimp and clothing made in factories called maquilas. Money from Hondurans abroad is a large part of the economy.

culture.text: The ruins of Copán, a Maya city famous for its carved stone monuments and hieroglyphic staircase, are a UNESCO site. The Garifuna people of the Caribbean coast have their own language and music. The Bay Islands are part of the second-largest barrier reef in the world.

sport.text: Football is the national passion. Honduras has played at three men's World Cups, in 1982, 2010 and 2014. In 1969, a short war between Honduras and El Salvador broke out after World Cup qualifiers between them.
